ge-world-kakheti.basis: Appellations of origin registered with Sakpatenti under the Law of Georgia on Appellations of Origin and Geographical Indications. Most are village micro-zones, shown here as points at the namesake village.
ge-world-kakheti.outline: Built from the administrative units that contain the area. The legal boundary follows other lines (roads, rivers, farms or altitude), so the real area is smaller.
ge-world-kakheti.atlas_note: Eastern Georgia along the Alazani valley, where most of the country's wine is made, including amber wines fermented with skins in buried clay qvevri, a method inscribed by UNESCO in 2013.

ge-world-tsinandali.basis: Appellations of origin registered with Sakpatenti under the Law of Georgia on Appellations of Origin and Geographical Indications. Most are village micro-zones, shown here as points at the namesake village.
ge-world-tsinandali.outline: Shown as a point at the place it is named after. The registered area is much smaller than any administrative unit, and its boundary is not yet available as open data.
ge-world-tsinandali.atlas_note: Village appellation in Kakheti for a dry white blend of Rkatsiteli and Mtsvane, named after the village of Tsinandali, home of the estate of the poet Alexander Chavchavadze.
